summary: 16 MB is not reachable for a functional router core; ~22-24 MB (arm64) is the realistic Ultra floor, ~7-8 MB xz on flash. RAM: private (anon) memory is already ~10-13 MB idle on desktop; most RSS is file-backed binary pages, reclaimable when the binary is on flash. A terminated mihomo connection can never be handed to the kernel forward path; the only DIRECT fast path is a pre-interception bypass of NEW connections whose verdict is provably IP-determinable. DIRECT TCP already uses splice(2); eBPF (XDP/TC/sk_lookup) is rejected, sockmap is at most an optional experiment; Rust components are rejected for MIPS profiles.

measurements.host: desktop x86_64 (CachyOS, Linux 7.3), Go 1.27.3; NOT router hardware
measurements.ultra_trial_note: Only the switch cases in adapter/parser.go and listener/parse.go were removed (17 outbounds, 13 inbounds) and with_gvisor dropped. Linker DCE still kept mipstack 416 KB (default TUN stack), quic-go 468 KB (vless xhttp-h3, DoH3/DoQ, QUIC sniffer), restls 356 KB, jls-tls 301 KB, protobuf 477 KB (GeoSite.dat), reedsolomon 237 KB (kcptun plugin). File-level build tags are needed for the rest.
measurements.rss_note: GOMAXPROCS=4 differs by <2 MB. Kernel memory of splice pipes is not in RSS and was not measured. Binary ran from tmpfs here, so file pages were RAM-backed; on a router with the binary on flash they are reclaimable page cache.

recommendations.title: Redefine the size target per profile
recommendations.decision: 16 MB is not reachable without dropping utls/REALITY, the QUIC stack and mihomo's HTTP fork. Proposed targets (stripped, arm64): Ultra <=24 MB, Lightweight <=31 MB, Performance = current lean 37 MB; MIPS +15%. Report xz size (flash) next to it: Ultra ~7-8 MB.
recommendations.confidence: medium (Ultra figure is an estimate from the trial build + per-module weights)

recommendations.title: Per-protocol build tags via stub files
recommendations.decision: Follow the existing tailscale/zerotier/easytier stub pattern: each protocol file gets //go:build !no_<proto> and a stub returning 'disabled at build time'; switches stay untouched (rebase-friendly). Patches needed beyond stubs: vless xhttp-h3, DoH3/DoQ, QUIC sniffer (for no_quic), shadowsocks plugins restls/kcptun, geodata protobuf (no_geosite_dat).

recommendations.title: Memory target defined as private memory
recommendations.decision: Measure and report RssAnon + kernel memory attributable to the core (pipes, sockets) as the RAM metric; report RssFile separately. Require the binary on flash (/usr/bin), never /tmp.

recommendations.title: First memory patches
recommendations.decision: (a) provider load concurrency 1-2 on low-memory profiles (one build-tagged file); (b) .mrs reader without per-element binary.Read allocations; (c) cap splice pipe size (e.g. 64-256 KiB) on low-memory profiles - needs a sing patch or a replace; (d) default GOMEMLIMIT/GOGC from /proc/meminfo when env is unset. Each measured on BPI-R4 before/after.

recommendations.title: DIRECT fast path = pre-interception bypass of NEW connections
recommendations.decision: No hand-back of terminated connections (impossible). The core marks a connection bypass-eligible only if its verdict is IP-determinable: the matched rule and every earlier rule that could match differently depend only on (dst IP, dst port, network[, src IP]); earlier non-determinable rules are allowed only if their outbound is the same DIRECT. Fake-IP connections and sniffed-host decisions are never eligible. Eligible keys go to an nft timeout set checked before interception; invalidation = flush set + conntrack delete by ct mark on every rule/config change and on core start/stop. Glue (clashwrt) owns the nft table; the core only emits verdicts (flow agent option C) behind a build tag.

recommendations.title: eBPF scope
recommendations.decision: Reject XDP, TC-BPF, sk_lookup, cgroup hooks for the core. sockmap verdict redirect for terminated DIRECT TCP: optional experiment only (Performance profile, build tag, raw-syscall loader preferred over cilium/ebpf +1.6 MB), adopted only if BPI-R4 shows a clear CPU win over splice. Fallback = splice (today's path).

recommendations.title: Rust components
recommendations.decision: Not for stages II-X: cgo breaks the pure-Go static cross-build and needs musl toolchains; Rust MIPS targets are tier 3; crypto on MIPS/ARMv7 is no faster; Go runtime overhead stays. meow-rs is used only as an external comparison baseline.

recommendations.title: CPU levers before code
recommendations.decision: Profile defaults and docs: tproxy/redirect or TUN system stack instead of mips/gvisor userspace stacks; ChaCha20-Poly1305 or VLESS-vision on MIPS/ARMv7 (no AES asm); tun.gso where the kernel allows; PGO only with a real MIPS/ARMv7 profile (4pda volunteers).

recommendations.title: Toolchain
recommendations.decision: Build with the newest stable Go (1.27.x) unless a benchmark shows a regression vs upstream's 1.26; record Go version in every BENCHMARKS row. CGO_ENABLED=0, non-PIE, -trimpath -s -w -buildid=.
